en: The Hymn to the Eightfold Nairātmyā O Goddess Nairātmyā, who possesses a nature that is without support, without form, and free from conceptual construction; O bestower of boons, homage be ever to you! (1)
I bow to the Mother of the Universe, who has one face and three eyes, whose tawny hair stands upright, and who holds a curved knife and a skull-cup in her hands.
I bow to her who is adorned with nine dances, who possesses a thousand faces and forms, the mistress of yoga who is attained through yoga, and whose nature is knowledge.
I bow to the Goddess, the Sovereign of the Universe, who is mounted upon a corpse, possessed of great splendor, the destroyer of all the wicked, and the remover of all sins. 4.
I bow to the eight yoginīs: Gaurī, Caurī, Vetālī, Ghasmarī, Pukkasī, Śabarī, Caṇḍālī, and Ḍombī. || 5 ||
I bow to the goddess, the beauty of the gods, who deludes the three worlds and destroys Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, Indra, and the four Māras.
I bow to the Goddess, the Mother of the Universe, whose body is adorned with a rosary, who originates from the seed-syllable *A*, and who is eternally devoted to meditation.
O Mother, I bow to you, Nairātmyā, who are beloved by all beings, the awakener of all mantras, and composed of all mantras. 8.
The Hymn in Eight Verses to Nairātmyā is completed.
